{{Current events|year=2020|month=01|day=22|content=

<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)]]
**[[Mitiga International Airport]], the only functioning airport in [[Libya]]'s capital [[Tripoli]], closes and a flight from [[Tunisia]] is diverted after forces loyal to [[Khalifa Haftar]] fire rockets toward the airport. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/tripoli-airport-closes-again-after-rocket-fire-idUSKBN1ZL1O6 (Reuters)] 

;Business and economy
*[[Elliott Management]], a prominent [[hedge fund]], has sold all its shares in the [[Hyundai Motor Group]] of South Korea. It had long quarreled with Hyundai's management, demanding more generous dividend pay-outs. Their departure from the shareholder ranks is likely welcomed by Hyundai executives. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hyundai-motor-elliott/activist-hedge-fund-elliott-sells-stakes-in-hyundai-motor-companies-paper-idUSKBN1ZL1DW (Reuters)] 

;Disasters and accidents
*Police in the [[Solomon Islands]] launch search operations to find nine people from a capsized boat near [[Isabel Province]]. Five men, two women and two children were on board. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/407867/search-for-9-missing-in-solomons-after-boat-capsized (RNZ)]
*A small plane crashes shortly after takeoff from [[Corona Municipal Airport]] in [[California]], killing all four on board. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/01/22/us/corona-plane-crash-california/index.html (CNN)]

;Health and environment
*[[2019–20 Wuhan coronavirus outbreak]]
**[[China|Chinese]] authorities [[quarantine]] the entire city of [[Wuhan]] to prevent the further spread of the novel [[coronavirus]] as the death toll rises to 17. Nobody in the city will be able to leave starting from 10 a.m. local time on January 23, and all public transport in the city is suspended. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/jan/22/coronavirus-china-measures-rein-spread-mutate-disease-death-toll (''The Guardian'')]

;International relations
*[[United Nations special rapporteur|UN special rapporteurs]] [[Agnès Callamard]] and [[David Kaye (law professor)|David Kaye]] demand an investigation into claims made by ''[[The Guardian]]'' yesterday that [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] [[Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia|Crown Prince]] [[Mohammad bin Salman]] ordered the 2018 hacking of [[Amazon (company)|Amazon]] CEO [[Jeff Bezos]]'s phone. The hack was allegedly done months before the [[assassination of Jamal Khashoggi]], who was employed at Bezos's newspaper ''[[The Washington Post]]'' and was a fierce critic of the Saudi government. The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Saudi Arabia)|Saudi Foreign Ministry]] dismisses the allegations as "absurd". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-people-bezos-saudi/u-n-experts-demand-probe-into-alleged-saudi-hack-of-amazon-boss-bezos-idUSKBN1ZL0C9?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Libyan peace process]]
**[[Algeria]] announces it will host a meeting with foreign ministers from six [[North Africa|North]] and [[sub-Saharan Africa]]n nations, all of whom share a border with Libya, following the [[Berlin]] peace summit to help strengthen support for a tentative peace deal to end the [[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Second Libyan Civil War]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/01/algeria-host-african-foreign-ministers-libya-conflict-200122154359602.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Law and crime
*[[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2020]]
**Eight people are shot, one fatally, following a dispute outside a [[McDonald's]] in [[Downtown Seattle|downtown]] [[Seattle]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]]. [https://www.seattletimes.com/seattle-news/crime/police-responding-to-shooting-near-4th-avenue-and-pine-street-reports-of-multiple-victims/ (''The Seattle Times'')]
*[[LGBT rights in South Korea]]
**A [[South Korea]]n [[transgender]] soldier says she will sue the [[Republic of Korea Armed Forces|armed forces]] after it discharged her. The soldier, Byun Hui-su, says she will take her claim "until the end, to the [[Supreme Court of South Korea|Supreme Court]]". [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-southkorea-military-lgbt/i-will-continue-to-fight-south-koreas-first-transgender-soldier-vows-to-oppose-dismissal-idUSKBN1ZL0QN (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Impeachment trial of Donald Trump]]
** The [[United States Senate]] hears opening statements in the [[impeachment]] trial of [[Donald Trump]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/impeachment-trial-live-updates/2020/01/22/3beb411e-3d05-11ea-8872-5df698785a4e_story.html (''The Washington Post'')] [http://dpaste.com/0S15GPE.txt (''The Washington Post'' via dpaste)] [https://archive.ph/OmFzZ (''The Washington Post'' via archive.ph)]
*[[President of Paraguay|Paraguayan President]] [[Mario Abdo Benítez]] is confirmed to have [[dengue fever]] amid a nationwide outbreak. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-paraguay-health-dengue/paraguays-president-abdo-contracts-dengue-fever-amid-outbreak-idUSKBN1ZL1U3 (Reuters)]
*[[Italy|Italian]] [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Italy)|Foreign Minister]] [[Luigi Di Maio]] resigns as leader of the ruling [[Five Star Movement]], as polls show the party losing support ahead of [[2020 Emilia-Romagna regional election|a regional election]] in [[Emilia-Romagna]] next Sunday. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51214954 (BBC)]
*[[Brexit]]
**The [[European Union (Withdrawal Agreement) Bill 2019–20|European Union Withdrawal Agreement Bill]] passes the [[House of Lords]] and is now awaiting [[royal assent]] to become law, finalizing the [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Withdrawal from the European Union|withdrawal]] from the [[European Union]] on 31 January 2020. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-51210602 (BBC)]

;Science and technology
*The [[Seattle metropolitan area]] becomes the first place in the United States to allow vote by [[smartphone]], which they authorized for a [[board of supervisors]] election in [[King County, Washington]] on February 11. [https://www.npr.org/2020/01/22/798126153/exclusive-seattle-area-voters-to-vote-by-smartphone-in-1st-for-u-s-elections (NPR)]

;Sports
*The [[National Football League|NFL's]] [[History of the Oakland Raiders|Oakland Raiders]] officially [[Oakland Raiders relocation to Las Vegas|relocate]] to [[Las Vegas]], and are now known as the [[Las Vegas Raiders]]. [https://www.businessinsider.com/the-raiders-have-moved-to-las-vegas-2020-1 (''Business Insider'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/raiders/2020/01/22/oakland-raiders-nfl-renamed-las-vegas-raiders/4548435002/?amp;amp (''USA Today'')]
